source_text: Breuioribus quoque epistulis non pigebit intendere. est sapor et in paucis. occiderant Iudaei prophetas suos. possum dicere: quid ad apostolum dei alterius et quidem optimi, qui nec suorum delicta damnare dicatur quique et ipse prophetas eosdem destruendo quodammodo perimat? quid mali admisit apud illum Israhel, si occidit quos et ille reprobauit, si prior inimicam in eos sententiam statuit? \'deliquit autem apud deum ipsorum\': is exprobrabit iniquitatem, ad quem pertinet laesus; certe quiuis alius quam aduersarius laesi. sed nec onerasset illos imputando etiam domini necem qui et dominum interfecerunt dicendo et prophetas suos, licet \'suos\' adiectio sit haeretici. quid enim tam acerbum, si alterius dei praedicatorem Christum interemerunt qui sui dei prophetas contrucidauerunt? status autem (est) exaggerationis, quod et dominum et famulos eius peremissent. denique si alterius dei Christum alterius prophetas peremerunt, aequauit impietatem, non exaggerauit. aequanda autem non fuit: ergo exaggerari non potuit, nisi in eundem deum commissa ex utroque titulo. ergo eiusdem dei Christus et prophetae. Quam autem sanctitatem nostram (uoluntatem dei\' dicat, ex contrariis, quae prohibet, agnoscere est — abstinere enim, inquit, a stupro, non a matrimonio; scire unumquemque uas suum in honore tractare. quomodo? dum non in libidine, qua gentes. libido autem nec apud gentes matrimonio adscribitur, sed extraordinarils et non naturalibus et portentosis luxuriae —: est turpitudini quaque et inmunditiae contraria, quae non matrimonium excludat, sed libidinem, quae uas nostrum in honore matrimonii tractet. hunc autem locum salua alterius, id est plenioris sanctitatis praelatione tractauerim, continentiam et uirginitatem nuptiis anteponens, sed non prohibitis. destructores enim dei nuptiarum, non sectatores castitatis retundo. Ait eos, qui remaneant in aduentum Christi cum eis, qui mortui in Christo primi resurgent, quod in nubibus auferentur in aerem obuiam domino. agnosco his iam tunc prospectis mirari substantias caelestes ipsam Hierusalem, quae sursum est, et per Esaiam pronuntiare: quinam huc uelut nubes uolant, tamquam columbae cum pullis ad me? hunc ascensum si Christus nobis praeparabit, ille erit Christus, de quo Osee: qui ascensum suum aedificat in caelos, utique sibi et suis. exinde a quo sperabo nunc, nisi a quo haec audiui ? Quem spiritum prohibet extingui et quas prophetias uetat nihil haberi? utique non creatoris spiritum nec creatoris prophetias secundum Marcionem. quae enim destruit, ipse iam extinxit et nihil fecit, nec potest prohibere quae ipse fecit. ergo incumbit Marcioni exhibere hodie apud ecclesiam suam exinde spiritum dei sui, qui non sit extinguendus, et prophetias, quae non sint nihil habendae. et si exhibuit quod putat, sciat nos quodcumque illud ad formam spiritalis et propheticae gratiae atque uirtutis prouocaturos, ut et futura praenuntiet et occulta cordis reuelet et sacramenta edisserat. cum nihil tale protulerit ac probarit, nos proferemus et spiritum et prophetias creatoris secundum ipsum praedicantes. atque ita constabit apostolus de quibus dixerit, de eis scilicet, quae futura erant in ecclesia eius dei, qui dum est, spiritus quoque eius operatur et promissio celebratur. Age nunc, qui salutem carnis abnuitis et, si quando corpus in huiusmodi praenominatur, aliud nescio quid interpretamini illud quam substantiam carnis, quomodo apostolus omnes in nobis substantias certis nominibus distinxit et omnes in uno uoto constituit salutis, optans, ut spiritus noster et corpus et anima sine querela in aduentu domini et salutificatoris nostri Christi conseruentur? nam et animam posuit et corpus, tam duas res quam diuersas. licet enim et anima I et] corpus sit aliquod suae qualitatis, sicut et spiritus, cum tamen et corpus et anima distincte nominantur, habet <autem) anima suum uocabulum proprium, non egens communi uocabulo corporis, id relinquitur carni, quae non nominata proprio, communi utatur necesse est. etenim aliam substantiam in homine non uideo post spiritum et animam, cui uocabulum corporis accommodetur praeter carnem, hanc totiens in corporis nomine intellegens, quotiens non nominatur; multo magis hic, cum quae dicitur corpus suo nomine appellatur.
pass_a_gloss: It will not be troublesome to also attend to the shorter epistles, for there is also flavor in a few words. The Jews had killed their own prophets. I can say: what does it pertain to the apostle of another God, and indeed a good one, who is said not to condemn the faults of his own, and who also destroys those prophets in a certain way? What evil did Israel commit with him, if it killed those whom he also rejected, if it established a hostile judgment against them first? 'However, it failed with their own God': he will reproach the iniquity to whom the injury pertains; certainly not anyone else but the adversary of the injured. But neither would he burden them by imputing the death of the Lord, who also killed the Lord, saying and the prophets, although 'their' is an addition of the heretic. For what is so bitter, if they killed the preacher of another God, Christ, who cut down the prophets of their own God? The fact that they killed both the Lord and his servants is a matter of exaggeration. Finally, if they killed Christ of another God and the prophets of another, they equalized the impiety, they did not exaggerate it. But it was not to be equalized: therefore, it could not be exaggerated, unless the offense was committed against the same God from both titles. Therefore, Christ and the prophets are of the same God. Moreover, what sanctity does he say is ours, from the contrary things that he prohibits, it is to recognize - for he says to abstain from fornication, not from marriage; to know that each one treats his vessel with honor. How? While not in lust, as the gentiles do. Lust, however, is not ascribed to marriage even among the gentiles, but to extraordinary and unnatural and monstrous luxuries - it is contrary to both turpitude and impurity, which does not exclude marriage but lust, which treats our vessel with honor in marriage. I will treat this passage, saving the preference of another, that is, fuller sanctity, by preferring continence and virginity to marriage, but not prohibiting them. For I censure the destroyers of God's marriages, not the followers of chastity. He says that those who remain until the coming of Christ, with those who died in Christ and will first rise again, will be taken up in the clouds into the air to meet the Lord. I recognize that they already then looked forward to marveling at the heavenly substances, at the very Jerusalem that is above, and pronounced through Isaiah: who are these who fly here like clouds, like doves with their young to me? If Christ prepares this ascent for us, he will be the Christ of whom Hosea says: who builds his ascent in the heavens, certainly for himself and his own. From whom shall I now hope, if not from him from whom I heard these things? Which spirit does he prohibit from being extinguished, and which prophecies does he forbid from being considered as nothing? Certainly not the spirit of the Creator nor the prophecies of the Creator, according to Marcion. For what he destroys, he has already extinguished and made nothing, nor can he prohibit what he himself made. Therefore, it is incumbent upon Marcion to exhibit today in his church the spirit of his God, which is not to be extinguished, and the prophecies that are not to be considered as nothing. And if he has exhibited what he thinks, let him know that we will provoke whatever that is to the form of spiritual and prophetic grace and virtue, so that it may predict future things and reveal the secrets of the heart and expound the sacraments. Since he has not produced and proven anything of the kind, we will produce the spirit and prophecies of the Creator, according to him, preaching. And thus it will be established that the apostle spoke about those things that were to come in the church of his God, who, while he exists, also works his spirit and fulfills his promise. Come now, you who deny the salvation of the flesh and, whenever the body is named in such a manner, interpret it as something other than the substance of the flesh, how does the apostle distinguish all substances in us with certain names and establishes all in one vow of salvation, wishing that our spirit and body and soul be preserved without complaint in the coming of our Lord and Savior Christ? For he also placed the soul and the body, as two distinct things. Although the soul and the body are something of their own quality, just like the spirit, yet since both the body and the soul are distinctly named, the soul has its own proper word, not needing the common word of the body, it leaves the flesh, which is not named by its own word, necessarily using the common word. Indeed, I do not see another substance in man after the spirit and the soul, to which the word 'body' can be applied, except the flesh, which I understand so many times in the name of the body, as many times as it is not named; much more so here, when what is said is called by its own name 'body'.

pass_b_english: It will not be troublesome to attend to the shorter epistles as well, for there is flavor even in a few words. The Jews killed their own prophets. I can ask: what concern is it of the apostle of another God — indeed a good one — who is said not to condemn the faults of his own people, and who also destroys those very prophets in a certain way? What evil did Israel commit against him, if it killed those whom he also rejected, if it passed a hostile judgment against them first? 'However, it failed with their own God': he will reproach the iniquity to whom the injury pertains; certainly no one but the adversary of the injured. But neither would he burden them by imputing even the death of the Lord, who also killed the Lord by their own confession and their own prophets — although 'their' is a heretic's addition. For what is so bitter, if they killed Christ, the preacher of another God, who slaughtered the prophets of their own God? The fact that they killed both the Lord and his servants is a matter of exaggeration. Finally, if they killed the Christ of another God and the prophets of another, they equalized the impiety; they did not exaggerate it. But it was not to be equalized: therefore it could not be exaggerated, unless the offense was committed against the same God on both counts. Therefore Christ and the prophets belong to the same God. (Isaiah)

I will treat this passage, saving the preference of another, that is, fuller sanctity, by preferring continence and virginity to marriage, but not prohibiting them. For I censure the destroyers of God's marriages, not the followers of chastity. He says that those who remain until the coming of Christ, together with those who died in Christ and will rise first, will be taken up in the clouds into the air to meet the Lord. I recognize that they already then looked forward to marveling at the heavenly substances, at the very Jerusalem that is above, and pronounced through Isaiah: 'Who are these who fly here like clouds, like doves with their young to me?' If Christ prepares this ascent for us, he will be the Christ of whom Hosea says: 'Who builds his ascent in the heavens, certainly for himself and his own.' From whom shall I now hope, if not from him from whom I heard these things? (Hosea)
